F-C13-01c.originalClaim: Test expected idempotency replay to bypass current authorization, but production correctly enforces JWT claims before replay lookup
F-C13-01c.correctedClaim: Test characterizes that replay authorization uses current JWT claims at replay time. Test obtains NEW JWT after role change, not using original JWT. Does not prove original JWT revocation.
F-C13-01c.coverageGap: Test does not characterize original JWT behavior after role change
F-C13-01c.sourceEvidence: Line 896: re-authenticates to obtain new JWT with updated role

F-C13-02.originalClaim: Test postpone dates violated business rule. API response omits plannedEndAt field.
F-C13-02.correctedClaim: Test characterizes: stale-version request gets 412, stores outcome, replay returns 412 with matching instance ID. Test does NOT prove whether replay re-evaluated version check or returned stored result without re-checking.
F-C13-02.coverageGap: Test does not prove replay skips version re-evaluation vs re-checks and gets same result
F-C13-02.sourceEvidence: Lines 833-836: compares instance IDs only, not full response immutability

F-C13-03.originalClaim: Test seeded SurveyAssignmentData (helper class) directly via DbContext.Add, but entity not registered in EF Core model
F-C13-03.correctedClaim: Test uses SurveyAssignmentData as value object for data construction, passes values to SurveyAssignment.Create() factory, adds via DbSet<SurveyAssignment>. SurveyAssignmentData is DTO/value object, not entity class.
F-C13-03.sourceEvidence: Lines 339-354: CreateSurveyAssignment returns value object, SurveyAssignment.Create() returns entity

F-C13-04.originalClaim: Inbox GET filters by recipient and projects correct fields
F-C13-04.sourceEvidence: Lines 86-100: asserts id, message, resourceId, read, occurredAt fields
